CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right knee pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient sustained a right knee injury one week ago at a trampoline park while with his wife. This was his first time visiting a trampoline park and he attended for fun. He heard a pop/snap when landing on the trampoline and experienced instant pain. Pain is localized to the lateral (outside) aspect of his right knee. He took Tylenol for pain relief but reports it did not help. He elevated the knee but did not apply ice or heat. He reports a limp when walking but is able to bear weight. He experiences pain with certain movements but reports decent range of motion in the knee.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg (patient reports taking most days)
Metformin 500 mg (patient reports taking)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient lives with his wife. This was his first visit to a trampoline park. He reports he does not work out regularly and has an inconsistent exercise regimen. He states he is reluctant to visit doctors. Regarding diet: he tries to watch what he eats and is watching his carbohydrates but is not counting calories or specific macros. He denies being on a specific diet such as keto and denies restricting salt.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Blood pressure 180/80
Cardiovascular: Heart with regular rate and rhythm, no murmur appreciated
Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally
Right Knee: Ecchymosis and edema noted along the lateral aspect. Mild tenderness to palpation on the lateral side, no tenderness on the medial side. No effusion noted. Patient able to bend and straighten knee. Gait reveals a limp. Patient able to bear weight on the extremity.

RESULTS
Right knee x-ray: No evidence of fracture or bony abnormality

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right knee pain - suspected lateral ligament strain
   - Prescribed meloxicam 15 mg daily for pain and swelling
   - Referred to physical therapy for muscle strengthening and injury prevention
   - Further imaging to be considered if pain persists
   - Counseled that this is a common injury that typically heals on its own

2. Hypertension
   - Continue lisinopril 20 mg
   - Ordered echocardiogram given concern about blood pressure control
   - Medication adjustment may be considered

3. Diabetes
   - Ordered A1C to assess long-term glucose control
   - Ordered lipid panel to guide potential medication adjustments
